qualification_gate: Serving live on the reference 2x DGX Spark pair 2026-08-19; output-correctness replay under speculation, LMCache cold-restart replay (byte-identical completion, planted-fact and indexer-desync probes), and heartbeat-longevity gates all passed (RESULTS.md). Throughput benchmarks beyond single-stream are pending.

hardware.fabric: direct ConnectX-7 200GbE RoCE between the pair; single rail (one port, rocep1s0f0, GID index 0)
hardware.storage: NVMe (ext4) for the LMCache L2 tier and JIT cache

image.source: FujitsuPolycom/sparkring runtime recipe (runtime/exl3-r7, pins.json is the component identity); published at ghcr.io/fujitsupolycom/gb10-vllm-serving
image.overlays: 8 bind mounts: three patch files (kernel_warmup.py from the SparkRing hotfix runtime/hotfixes/deployed-r34-20260810, quack/copy_utils.py and quack/layout_utils.py for the quack/cutlass version skew, and the tvm-ffi directory) plus model, cache, HuggingFace-cache and transport-library mounts. leg3pair.binds ships the reference pair's full 51-mount capture; the other 43 are inert at TP2 and were verified removable.
image.note: The runtime is not built by this profile; it is the SparkRing project's image plus three patch files, launched with the deltas recorded here. The published image is a flattened single-layer capture carrying no build steps: its component identity is in its own labels (vLLM commit fcc61414 from local-inference-lab/vllm, b12x commit 284a2eae, torch 2.12.0+cu132, NCCL 2.30.4) and in runtime/exl3-r7/pins.json in FujitsuPolycom/sparkring, whose builder overlay is on a separate branch. Pulling the registry reference yields image ID sha256:02881d5229d4f4d1cbba0cf40537492a2a505b9d4e43bbfe9a0b2a7bd0584513.

runtime.engine: vLLM inside the image at /opt/venv (SparkRing pins: local-inference-lab/vllm + integration patch)

speculative_config.note: depth 5 is the checkpoint's dspark_block_size and the engine's minimum; depth 7 serves but measures 14% slower

runtime.removed_from_ring_spec: SPARK_TP4_* / VLLM_SPARK_TP4_* custom-transport env (source admits only world_size==4); NCCL 4-cycle settings (SKIP_TREE_CONNECT, ALGO=Ring, NCHANNELS=4, subnet-aware routing)

lmcache.code: local-inference-lab/LMCache branch release/v0.5.2-glm52-dcp-base, head a128b2e2, tree e045d729bc5c, plus the heartbeat dead-guard patch; wheel 0.5.3.dev51 built against the image's torch 2.12 and installed at container start over the image's 0.5.2+glm52dcp4.1
lmcache.topology: one MP server per rank, inside the engine's container (shared lifecycle removes the stale-CUDA-IPC restart hazard); ZMQ port 6570, metrics 6580
lmcache.l1: 4 GiB lazy, LRU, as shipped in leg3pair-inner.sh, qualified for serving and for long-context prefill headroom: a 65,536-token prefill leaves 11 GB available per node against 12.5 GB at idle, where an 8 GiB buffer reached the 7-8 GB at which the engine core was killed. Consequence of the smaller buffer: a prefix stages into L1 before a lookup counts an L2 hit, and the external prefix cache hit rate reads 33.7% at 65,536 tokens against 97.2% at 24,000, bounding the staging reach between those lengths and matching a per-token footprint estimate of 50,000 to 67,000 tokens. Prefixes past the reach recompute instead of restoring. Cells in RESULTS.md marked as taken under an 8 GiB buffer predate this value.
lmcache.l2: fs_native, 200 GiB per rank, buffered I/O, path encodes checkpoint revision and geometry (lmcache-l2-dsv4-0731-spec-b256)

benchmarks.note: Client-observed unless stated; conditions in RESULTS.md. Figures in this block were measured with an 8 GiB LMCache L1 buffer, where a 64K prefill exhausted node memory and the engine core was killed. The shipped 4 GiB buffer was measured separately: see single_stream_decode_tok_s_at_4gib_l1 and longctx_min_avail_gb_at_4gib_l1 below and the corresponding RESULTS.md section. Coding output decodes about 1.6x faster than prose because speculative acceptance rises on structured content.
